text: A typical year has 365 days. This count refers to the common year in the Gregorian calendar, which is the civil calendar used internationally today. The context of this fact is rooted in the Earth's orbital period around the Sun, known as a tropical year, which is approximately 365.2422 days. To account for the extra fraction of a day, leap years are added every four years (with some exceptions) to keep the calendar synchronized with the astronomical seasons. The provided evidence regarding the Big Bang theory and the expansion of the universe does not alter this terrestrial calendar definition, as it pertains to cosmological history rather than the mechanics of Earth's orbit or human timekeeping systems.
